mn82:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering in the Kuru country together with a large Sangha of bhikkhus. He eventually arrived at Thullakoṭṭhita, a Kuru town.
mn82:2.1: The divine caste householders of Thullakoṭṭhita heard:
mn82:2.2: ‘The monk Gotama, it seems a son of the Sakyans who went forth from a Sakyan clan, has been wandering in the Kosalan country with a large Sangha of bhikkhus and has come to Sālā.
mn82:2.3: Now a good report of Master Gotama has been spread to this effect.
mn82:2.4: “That Blessed One is such since he is Arahant and Fully Enlightened, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds, incomparable teacher of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and men, enlightened, blessed.
mn82:2.5: He describes this world with its Māras, and its (Brahmā) Divinities, this generation with its monks and divines, with its kings and its men, which he has himself realized through direct knowledge.
mn82:2.6: He teaches a Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle and good in the end with (the right) meaning and phrasing, he affirms a life divine that is utterly perfect and pure.”
mn82:2.7: It is good to see such Arahants.’
mn82:3.1: Then the divine caste householders of Thullakoṭṭhita went to the Blessed One and some paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side; some exchanged greetings with him, and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished, sat down at one side; some raised their hands palms together in salutation to the Blessed One and sat down at one side; some pronounced their name and clan in the Blessed One’s presence and sat down at one side; some kept silent and sat down at one side.
mn82:3.2: When they were seated, the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused and encouraged them with talk on the Dhamma.
mn82:4.1: Now at that time a clansman called Raṭṭhapāla, the son of the leading clan in that same Thullakoṭṭhita, was sitting in the assembly.
mn82:4.3: ‘As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is not possible while living in a household to lead the life divine utterly perfect and pure as a polished shell.
mn82:4.4: Suppose I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and went forth from the home life into homelessness?’
mn82:5.1: Then the brahmin householders of Thullakoṭṭhita, having been instructed, urged, roused and encouraged by the Blessed One with talk on the Dhamma, and delighted in his words and agreeing, rose from their seats, and after paying homage to him, they departed keeping him on their right.
mn82:6.1: Soon after they had gone the clansman Raṭṭhapāla went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said to the Blessed One:
mn82:6.2: ‘Venerable sir, as I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is not possible while living in a household, to lead the life divine as perfect and pure as a polished shell.
mn82:6.3: Venerable sir, I want to shave off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:6.4: I would receive the Going-forth under the Blessed One and I would receive the Full Admission.’
mn82:6.6: ‘Are you permitted by your parents, Raṭṭhapāla, to go forth from the home life into homelessness?’
mn82:6.8: ‘Tathāgatas do not give the Going-forth without the parents’ permission, Raṭṭhapāla.’
mn82:6.9: ‘Venerable sir, I shall see to it that my parents permit me to go forth from the home life into homelessness.’
mn82:7.1: Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the Blessed One, (he left) keeping him on his right. He went to his parents and told them:
mn82:7.2: ‘Mother and father, as I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is impossible while living in a household to lead the life divine as perfect and pure as a polished shell.
mn82:7.3: I want to shave off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:7.4: Give me permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness.’
mn82:7.5: When this was said his parents replied:
mn82:7.6: ‘Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you, being an only son and dear and precious to us, have been educated to pleasure, brought up to pleasure.
mn82:7.7: Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you know nothing of suffering.
mn82:7.8: In case of your death we should lose you willy-nilly;
mn82:7.9: but why should we give you our permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?’
mn82:7.11: For the third time the clansman Raṭṭhapāla said to his parents:
mn82:7.12: ‘Mother and father … give me permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness.’
mn82:7.15: For the third time his parents replied:
mn82:7.16: ‘Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you, being an only son and dear and precious to us, have been educated to pleasure, brought up to pleasure.
mn82:7.17: Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you know nothing of suffering.
mn82:7.18: In case of your death we should lose you willy-nilly;
mn82:7.19: but why should we give you our permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?’
mn82:7.21: Then, not getting his parents’ (permission) for the Going-forth, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla lay down there on the bare floor, (thinking:)
mn82:7.22: ‘Right here I shall either die or get the Going-forth’.
mn82:8.1: Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla’s parents said to him:
mn82:8.2: ‘Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you, being an only son and dear and precious to us, have been educated to pleasure, brought up to pleasure.
mn82:8.3: Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you know nothing of suffering.
mn82:8.5: but why should we give you our permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?
mn82:8.6: Get up, dear Raṭṭhapāla, eat, drink and be merry;
mn82:8.7: enjoy eating, drinking, being merry, indulging sensual desires and making merit.
mn82:8.8: We do not permit you to go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:8.9: In case of your death we should lose you willy-nilly:
mn82:8.10: but why should we give you our permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?’
mn82:8.11: When this was said the clansman Raṭṭhapāla was silent.

mn82:8.15: ‘Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you, being an only son …

mn82:10.9: In case of your death they would lose you willy-nilly;
mn82:10.10: but why should they give you their permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness while you are still living?’
mn82:10.11: When this was said, the clansman Raṭṭhapāla was silent.

mn82:10.14: ‘Good Raṭṭhapāla, you, being an only son …

mn82:11.1: Then the clansman Raṭṭhapāla’s friends went to his parents and said to them:
mn82:11.2: ‘Mother and father, this clansman Raṭṭhapāla has lain down there on the bare floor, (thinking:)
mn82:11.3: “Right here I shall either die or get the Going-forth.”
mn82:11.4: Now if you do not give him your permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness, he will die there.
mn82:11.5: But if you give him your permission, you will see him after he has gone forth.
mn82:11.6: And if he does not enjoy the Going-forth, what else can he do then but return here?
mn82:11.7: So give him your permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness.’
mn82:11.8: ‘Then we give the clansman Raṭṭhapāla permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:11.9: But when he has gone forth, he must visit his parents.’
mn82:11.10: So the clansman Raṭṭhapāla’s friends went to him and told him:
mn82:11.11: ‘You are permitted by your parents to go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:11.12: But when you have gone forth, you must visit your parents.’
mn82:12.1: The clansman Raṭṭhapāla then got up, and when he had gained strength, he went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said:
mn82:12.2: ‘Venerable sir, I have my parents’ permission to go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:12.3: Let the Blessed One give me the Going-forth.’
mn82:13.1: So the clansman Raṭṭhapāla received the Going-forth under the Blessed One, and he received the Full Admission.
mn82:13.2: Then soon after the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s Full Admission, when he had been fully admitted a fortnight, the Blessed One, having stayed at Thullakoṭṭhita as long as he chose, set out to go by stages to Sāvatthi.
mn82:13.3: Wandering by stages, he at length arrived at Sāvatthi.
mn82:13.4: There he lived in Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove. Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn82:14.1: Meanwhile, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, the venerable Raṭṭhapāla, by realization himself with direct knowledge here and now entered upon and abode in that supreme goal of the life divine for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:14.2: He knew directly: ‘Birth is ended, the life divine has been lived, what was to be done is done, there is no more of this to come.’
mn82:14.3: And the venerable Raṭṭhapāla became one of the Arahants.
mn82:15.1: Then the venerable Raṭṭhapāla went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, he said:
mn82:15.2: ‘Venerable sir, I wish to see my parents, if I have the Blessed One’s permission.’
mn82:15.3: Then encompassing mind with mind the Blessed One directed his attention to the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s thought.
mn82:15.5: ‘The clansman Raṭṭhapāla is incapable of forsaking the training and reverting to what he has abandoned,’ he told him:
mn82:15.6: ‘It is time for you, Raṭṭhapāla, to do as you think fit.’
mn82:16.1: The venerable Raṭṭhapāla rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the Blessed One, (he departed), keeping him on his right. Then he set his resting place in order, and taking his bowl and (outer) robe, he set out to go by stages to Thullakoṭṭhita.
mn82:16.2: Wandering by stages, he eventually arrived at Thullakoṭṭhita.
mn82:16.3: There he lived in Thullakoṭṭhita in King Koravya’s Migācira (Garden).
mn82:16.4: Then, when it was morning, he dressed, and taking his bowl and (outer) robe, he went into Thullakoṭṭhita for alms.
mn82:16.5: As was wandering from house to house he came to his own father’s house.
mn82:17.1: Now on that occasion the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father was sitting in the hall of the central door having his hair dressed.
mn82:17.2: He saw the venerable Raṭṭhapāla coming in the distance.
mn82:17.3: When he saw him, he said:
mn82:17.4: ‘Our only son who was dear and precious to us was made to go forth by these monkish shavelings.’
mn82:17.5: Then the venerable Raṭṭhapāla got neither gifts nor polite refusal,
mn82:17.6: and instead he got only abuse.
mn82:18.1: A bondswoman belonging to one of his relatives was about to throw away some stale porridge.
mn82:18.3: ‘Sister, if that is stuff to be thrown away, then pour it into my bowl here.’
mn82:18.4: While she was doing so, she recognized the characteristics of his hands, his feet and his voice.
mn82:18.5: Then she went to his mother and said:
mn82:18.6: ‘My goodness, my lady! Do you know that
mn82:18.7: my lord’s son Raṭṭhapāla has arrived?’
mn82:18.8: ‘Gracious! If what you say is true, you are a bondswoman no more!’
mn82:18.9: Then the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s mother went to his father and said:
mn82:18.10: ‘My goodness, householder! Do you know that
mn82:18.11: they say that the clansman Raṭṭhapāla has arrived?’
mn82:19.1: Just then the venerable Raṭṭhapāla was eating the stale porridge by the wall of a certain (shelter).
mn82:19.2: His father went to him and said:
mn82:19.3: ‘Raṭṭhapāla, my dear, surely there is …  and you will be eating stale porridge!
mn82:19.4: Is there not your own house to go to?’
mn82:19.5: ‘How should we, householder, who have gone forth from the home life into homelessness, have a house?
mn82:19.7: We went to your home but we got neither gifts nor polite refusal there,
mn82:19.9: ‘Come, Raṭṭhapāla dear, let us go to the house.’
mn82:19.10: ‘Enough, householder, I have finished my meal for today.’
mn82:19.12: The venerable Raṭṭhapāla accepted in silence.
mn82:20.1: Then knowing that his son had accepted, he went back to his own house. He had gold and bullion made into a large heap and covered with mats. Then he told the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s former wives:
mn82:20.2: ‘Come, daughters-in-law, dress yourselves up in the way in which Raṭṭhapāla used to hold you most dear and precious.’
mn82:21.1: When the night was ended, the venerable Raṭṭhapāla’s father had good food of various kinds prepared in his own house, and he had the time announced to the venerable Raṭṭhapāla:
mn82:21.2: ‘It is time, dear Raṭṭhapāla, the meal is ready.’
mn82:22.1: Then, it being morning, the venerable Raṭṭhapāla dressed, and taking his bowl and (outer) robe, he went to his own father’s house, and he sat down on the seat made ready. Then his father had the pile of gold and bullion uncovered, and he said:
mn82:22.2: ‘Raṭṭhapāla dear, this is your maternal fortune; your paternal fortune is another and your ancestral fortune is yet another.
mn82:22.3: Ratṭhapāla dear, you can use the wealth and make merit.
mn82:22.4: Come then, renounce the training, return to what you have abandoned, use the wealth and make merit.’
mn82:22.5: ‘Householder, if you would do as I say, then have this pile of gold and bullion loaded on carts and carried away to be dumped in the River Ganges in midstream.
mn82:22.7: Because, householder, for you it will be a source of sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair.’
mn82:23.1: The venerable Ratṭhapāla’s former wives clasped both his feet, saying to him:
mn82:23.2: ‘What are they like, my lord, the nymphs for whose sake you lead the life divine?’
mn82:23.3: ‘We do not lead the life divine for the sake of nymphs, sisters.’
mn82:23.4: ‘My lord’s son Ratṭhapāla calls us “sisters”,’ (they cried) and they fell swooning on the spot.
mn82:24.1: Then the venerable Ratṭhapāla told his father:
mn82:24.2: ‘Householder, if there is a meal to be given, then give it.
mn82:24.4: ‘Eat then, dear Ratṭhapāla. The meal is ready.’
mn82:24.5: Then with his own hands the venerable Ratṭhapāla’s father served and satisfied him with the various kinds of food.
mn82:24.6: When the venerable Ratṭhapāla had no longer the bowl in his hand, he stood up and uttered these stanzas:
mn82:25.2: A body built up out of sores,
mn82:25.5: Behold a figure here pranked out,
mn82:25.7: A skeleton wrapped up in skin,
mn82:25.10: And powder smeared upon its face,
mn82:25.12: but not a seeker of the Further Shore.
mn82:25.13: Its hair is dressed in eightfold plaits
mn82:25.14: And unguent smeared upon its eyes,
mn82:25.16: but not a seeker of the Further Shore.
mn82:25.20: but not a seeker of the Further Shore.
mn82:25.21: The deer-hunter sets well the snare
mn82:25.22: But the deer springs not the trap;
mn82:25.23: We ate the bait, and we depart
mn82:26.1: When the venerable Raṭṭhapāla had stood up and uttered these stanzas, he went to King Koravya’s Migācira (Garden) and sat down at the root of a tree for the day’s abiding.
mn82:27.1: Then King Koravya addressed Migava thus:
mn82:27.2: ‘Good Migava, get the Migācira (Garden) tidied up, to the pleasure garden
mn82:27.3: so that we may go to see a pleasing spot.’
mn82:27.4: ‘Yes, sir,’ he replied. Now while he was having the Migācira (Garden) tidied up, he saw the venerable Raṭṭhapāla seated at the root of a tree for the day’s abiding.
mn82:27.5: When he saw him, he went to the King Koravya and told him:
mn82:27.6: ‘Sire, the Migācira (Garden) has been tidied up.
mn82:27.7: And the clansman called Raṭṭhapāla is there, the son of the leading clan in this same Thullakoṭṭhita, of whom you have always spoken highly; he is seated at the foot of a tree for the day’s abiding.’
mn82:27.8: ‘Then, good Migava, enough of the pleasure garden for today.
mn82:27.9: Now we shall pay honour to that Master Raṭṭhapāla.’
mn82:28.1: Then, (saying:) ‘Give away all food of any kind that has been prepared there,’ King Koravya had a number of state carriages got ready, and mounting a state carriage, he drove out from Thullakoṭṭhita with the full pomp of royalty to see the venerable Raṭṭhapāla.
mn82:28.2: He went thus as far as the road was passable for carriages, and then he got down from his carriage and went forward on foot with a following of the most eminent (officials) to where the venerable Raṭṭhapāla was. He exchanged greetings with the venerable Raṭṭhapāla, and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he stood at one side. Then he said:
mn82:28.3: ‘Here is an elephant rug. Let Master Raṭṭhapāla be seated on it.’
mn82:28.4: ‘There is no need, great king. (Please) sit down.
mn82:28.5: I am sitting on my own mat.’
mn82:28.6: King Koravya sat down on a seat made ready. When he had done so, he said:
mn82:29.1: ‘Master Raṭṭhapāla, there are four kinds of loss after undergoing which some people here shave off their hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth and go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:29.3: They are loss through ageing, loss through sickness, loss of property and loss of relatives.
mn82:30.2: Here someone is old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life, and come to the last stage.
mn82:30.4: “I am old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life and come to the last stage.
mn82:30.5: It is no more possible for me to acquire unacquired properties or to augment properties already acquired.
mn82:30.6: Suppose I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth and went forth from the home life into homelessness?”
mn82:30.7: Undergoing that loss through ageing, he shaves off his hair and beard, puts on the yellow cloth and goes forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:30.8: This is called loss through ageing.
mn82:30.9: But Master Raṭṭhapāla is now still young, a black-haired boy endowed with the blessing of youth, in the first phase of life.
mn82:30.10: Master Raṭṭhapāla has nothing of loss through ageing.
mn82:30.11: What has he known or seen or heard that he has gone forth from the home life into homelessness?’
mn82:31.2: Here someone is afflicted, suffering and gravely ill.
mn82:31.4: “I am afflicted, suffering and gravely ill.
mn82:31.5: It is no more possible for me to acquire unacquired properties or to augment properties already acquired.
mn82:31.6: Suppose I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and went forth from the home life into homelessness?
mn82:31.7: Undergoing that loss through sickness, he shaves off …
mn82:31.8: This is called loss through sickness.
mn82:31.9: But Master Raṭṭhapāla has now no affliction or ailment, having a good digestion that is neither too cool nor nor too warm but medium.
mn82:31.10: Master Raṭṭhapāla has nothing of loss through sickness.
mn82:31.11: What has he known or seen or heard that he has gone forth from the home life into homelessness?
mn82:32.2: Here someone is rich with great wealth and great property.
mn82:32.3: Gradually those properties of his dwindle away.
mn82:32.5: “Formerly I was rich with great wealth and great property.
mn82:32.6: Gradually those properties of mine have dwindled away.
mn82:32.7: It is no more possible for me to acquire … into homelessness?”
mn82:32.8: Suppose I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and went forth from the home life into homelessness
mn82:32.9: Undergoing that loss of property, he shaves off …
mn82:32.10: This is called loss of property.
mn82:32.11: But Master Raṭṭhapāla is the son of the leading clan in this same Thullakoṭṭhita.
mn82:32.12: Master Raṭṭhapāla has nothing of that loss of wealth.
mn82:32.13: What has he known or seen or heard that he has gone forth from the home life into homelessness?
mn82:33.2: Here someone has many friends and companions, relatives and kin.
mn82:33.3: Gradually those relatives of his dwindle away.
mn82:33.5: “Formerly I had many friends and companions, relatives and kin.
mn82:33.6: Gradually those relatives of mine have dwindled away.
mn82:33.7: It is no more possible for me to acquire … into homelessness?”
mn82:33.8: Suppose I shaved off my hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth, and went forth from the home life into homelessness?’
mn82:33.9: Undergoing that loss of relatives, he shaves off …
mn82:33.10: This is called loss of relatives.
mn82:33.11: But Master Raṭṭhapāla has many friends and companions, relatives and kin in this same Thullakoṭṭhita.
mn82:33.12: Master Raṭṭhapāla has nothing of that loss of relatives.
mn82:33.13: What has he known or seen or heard that he has gone forth from the home life into homelessness?
mn82:34.1: ‘Master Raṭṭhapāla, these are four kinds of loss after undergoing which some people here shave off their hair and beard, put on the yellow cloth and go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:34.2: Master Raṭṭhapāla has none of these.
mn82:34.3: What has he known or seen or heard that he has gone forth from the home life into homelessness?’
mn82:35.1: ‘Great king, there are four summaries of Dhamma which have been given by the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, knowing and seeing and hearing which I went forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:36.1: ‘ “(Life in) any world has no lastingness, and is led on”:
mn82:36.2: this is the first summary of the Dhamma given by the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, knowing and seeing and hearing which I went forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:36.3: ‘ “(Life in) any world has no shelter and no protector”:
mn82:36.4: this is the second summary … into homelessness.
mn82:36.5: ‘ “(Life in) any world has nothing of its own; it has to leave all and pass on”:
mn82:36.7: ‘ “(Life in) any world is incomplete, insatiate and the slave of craving”:
mn82:36.8: this is the fourth summary … knowing and seeing and hearing which I went forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn82:37.1: ‘Great king, these are the four summaries of the Dhamma which have been given by the Blessed One … into homelessness.’
mn82:38.1: ‘ “(Life in) any world has no lastingness, and is led on”,
mn82:38.3: but how should the meaning of that statement be regarded?’
mn82:38.4: ‘How do you conceive this, great king,
mn82:38.5: when you were twenty years old and twenty-five years old, were you an expert rider of elephants, an expert horseman, an expert charioteer, an expert bowman, an expert swordsman, strong in thigh and arm, sturdy and used to wars?’
mn82:38.7: Sometimes I wonder if I had supernormal power: I do not see that it was quite the same as my own power.’
mn82:38.8: ‘How do you conceive this, great king,
mn82:38.9: are you now as strong in thigh and arm, as sturdy and as used to wars?’
mn82:38.11: Now I am old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life and come to the last stage. My years have turned eighty.
mn82:38.12: Sometimes I mean to put my foot here and I put my foot somewhere else.’
mn82:38.13: ‘Great king, it was on account of this that the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, said:
mn82:38.14: “(Life in) any world has no lastingness and is led on”,
mn82:38.15: and when I knew and saw and heard that, I went forth from the home life into homelessness.’
mn82:38.16: ‘It is wonderful, Master Raṭṭhapāla, it is marvellous
mn82:38.17: how well that has been expressed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened.
mn82:38.18: “(Life in) any world has no lastingness and is led on”,
mn82:39.1: ‘Master Raṭṭhapāla, there exist in this court elephant troops and cavalry and chariot troops and infantry, which will serve to subdue any threats to us.
mn82:39.2: Now “(Life in) any world has no shelter and no protector”
mn82:39.4: but how should the meaning of that statement be regarded?’
mn82:39.5: ‘How do you conceive this, great king,
mn82:39.7: ‘I have a latent wind sickness, Master Raṭṭhapāla.
mn82:39.8: Sometimes my friends and companions, my relatives and kin, stand around me, (saying):
mn82:39.9: “Now King Koravya is about to die, now King Koravya is about to die!”’
mn82:39.10: ‘How do you conceive this, great king,
mn82:39.11: can you have it thus with your friends and companions, your relatives and kin:
mn82:39.12: “Come, my good friends and companions, my relatives and kin, do all of you present share out this feeling (of pain) so that I may feel less feeling (of pain)”,
mn82:39.13: or do you have to feel that feeling (of pain) yourself alone?’
mn82:39.14: ‘I cannot have it thus, Master Raṭṭhapāla,
mn82:39.16: I have to feel that feeling of pain alone.’
mn82:39.17: ‘Great king, it was on account of this that the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, said:
mn82:39.18: “(Life in) any world has no shelter and no protector”;
mn82:39.19: and when I knew and saw and heard that, I went forth from the home life into homelessness.’
mn82:39.22: “(Life in) any world has no shelter and protector”,
mn82:40.1: ‘Master Raṭṭhapāla, there exists in this court ample gold and bullion stored away in cellars and laid up in attics.
mn82:40.2: Now “(Life in) any world has nothing of its own; it has to leave all and pass on”
mn82:40.4: but how should the meaning of that statement be regarded?’
mn82:40.5: ‘How do you conceive this, great king,
mn82:40.6: you are now furnished and invested with the five cords of sensual desires and enjoy them, but will you be able to have it of the life to come:
mn82:40.7: “May I be likewise furnished and invested with these five cords of sensual desires and enjoy them”, or will others take over this property, while you will have to pass on according to your kammas?’
mn82:40.8: ‘I cannot have it thus, Master Raṭṭhapāla.
mn82:40.10: On the contrary, others will take over this property, while I shall have to pass on according to my kammas.’
mn82:40.11: ‘Great king, it was on account of this that the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, said:
mn82:40.12: “(Life in) any world has nothing of its own; it has to leave all and pass on”;
mn82:40.13: and when I knew and heard that, I went forth from the home life to homelessness.’
mn82:40.16: “(Life in) any world has nothing of its own; it has to leave all and pass on”,
mn82:41.1: ‘Now, “(Life in) any world is incomplete, insatiate, and the slave of craving”
mn82:41.3: but how should the meaning of that statement be regarded?’
mn82:41.4: ‘How do you conceive this, Great King,
mn82:41.5: do you live in the rich Kuru country as its owner?’
mn82:41.7: ‘How do you conceive this, great king?
mn82:41.8: If a trustworthy and reliable man came to you from the east
mn82:41.10: “Please to know, great king, that I come from the east,
mn82:41.11: and there I saw a large country powerful and rich, very populous and crowded with men;
mn82:41.12: there are plenty of elephant troops there, plenty of cavalry, plenty of chariot troops and plenty of infantry;
mn82:41.13: there is plenty of ivory there,
mn82:41.14: and plenty of gold and bullion both unworked and worked,
mn82:41.15: and there are plenty of women for wives.
mn82:41.16: With such and such a force you can conquer it.
mn82:41.17: Conquer it then, great king.” How would you act?’
mn82:41.18: ‘We should conquer it and live there as its owner, Master Raṭṭhapāla.’
mn82:41.19: ‘How do you conceive this, great king,
mn82:41.20: if a trustworthy and reliable man came to you from the west …
mn82:41.33: ‘We should conquer it too and live there as its owner, Master Raṭṭhapāla.’
mn82:41.34: ‘Great king, it was on account of this that the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, said:
mn82:41.35: “(Life in) any world is incomplete, insatiate and the slave of craving”,
mn82:41.36: and when I knew and saw and heard that, I went forth from the home life into homelessness.’
mn82:41.38: ‘It is wonderful, Master Raṭṭhapāla, it is marvellous how well that has been expressed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Full Enlightened:
mn82:41.39: “(Life in) any world is incomplete, insatiate and the slave of craving”,
mn82:42.1: That is what the venerable Raṭṭhapāla said.
mn82:42.2: And having said that he said further:
mn82:42.3: I see men wealthy in the world, who yet
mn82:42.4: Give not, from ignorance, their gathered riches;
mn82:42.5: But greedily will hoard away their wealth,
mn82:42.6: Through longing for still further sensual pleasures.
mn82:42.7: A king who has by force conquered the earth
mn82:42.8: And even lords the land the ocean bounds
mn82:42.9: Is yet unsated with the sea’s near shore
mn82:42.10: And hungers for its further shore as well.
mn82:42.11: Most other men as well, not just a king,
mn82:42.13: (With plans) still incomplete they leave the corpse;
mn82:42.14: Desires remain unsated in the world.
mn82:42.15: His relatives lament him, rend their hair,
mn82:42.16: Crying “Ah me! Alas! Our love is dead!”
mn82:42.17: Then bear away the body wrapped in shrouds
mn82:42.18: To place it on a pyre and burn it there.
mn82:42.19: and prodded with stakes he burns,
mn82:42.20: Clad in single shroud, he leaves behind His property,
mn82:42.21: And as he died, no relatives or kin
mn82:42.22: Or friends could offer refuge to him here.
mn82:42.23: The while his heirs annex his wealth,
mn82:42.24: this being must now pass on according to his kammas;
mn82:42.25: And as he dies no thing can follow him:
mn82:42.26: Nor child nor wife nor wealth nor royal estate.
mn82:42.27: Longevity is not acquired with wealth
mn82:42.28: Nor can prosperity banish old age;
mn82:42.29: Short is this life, as all the sages say,
mn82:42.30: Eternity it knows not, only change.
mn82:42.31: The rich man and the poor man both shall feel (Death’s) touch,
mn82:42.32: as do the fool and sage alike;
mn82:42.33: But while the fool lies stricken by his folly,
mn82:42.34: No sage will ever tremble at the touch.
mn82:42.36: The goal can here be gained, than any wealth;
mn82:42.37: For men through different lives in ignorance
mn82:42.38: Do evil, while they fail to reach the goal.
mn82:42.39: As one goes to the womb and the next world,
mn82:42.40: Renewing the successive round, so another
mn82:42.41: With no more understanding, trusting him,
mn82:42.42: Goes also to the womb and the next world.
mn82:42.43: Just as robber caught in burglary
mn82:42.44: By his own kamma’s marked a miscreant,
mn82:42.45: So people are after death, in the next world
mn82:42.46: By their own kammas marked as miscreants.
mn82:42.47: For sense desires so mind-alluring, sweet,
mn82:42.48: In many a different way disturb the mind;
mn82:42.49: Seeing the danger in these sense desires
mn82:42.50: So I went forth to homelessness, O king.
mn82:42.51: Men whether young or old, like fruits of trees
mn82:42.52: Fall when the body’s break-up comes about;
mn82:42.53: That too I saw, and so went forth, O king,
mn82:42.54: Better by far the monk’s state assured.
